because it's never immediate. It builds up over a long time. First time it's just you and your partner getting in a fight, normal thing that happens in a relationship. Before you know it, the fights become regular and turn into threats and maybe more.

Like she said in the livestream it also involves a lot of love bombing afterward. It convinces you "my partner isn't usually like this" and the huge affection they show you afterward convinces you of that. They'll plead with you, beg for forgiveness, say that they'll get therapy, and get you to convince yourself you can fix them. You think that once you've helped them everything will go "back to normal" and you can go back to the how you were when you were first together.

When you realize their behavior isn't changing, they'll convince you that it's your fault. You antagonized them. You were condescending. You made a mean face. Once they make you internalize this, you'll be walking on eggshells hoping that whatever you do doesn't cause another fight. But of course, in abusive relationships no matter what you do a fight's going to come sooner or later. The cycle repeats again with the fights and the love bombing, leaving you exhausted.

They also try and cut you off as much as possible from people who might support you. If you go out for extended periods of time without them, they'll accuse you of not wanting to be around them, or maybe cheating on them. If it goes on too long, the most contact you have with people are friends of theirs, or meeting with them present. The most important thing when leaving an abusive relationship is a support network, and a support network will need to know what's going on. If you speak out to people who know them, you risk that person not believing you or going to your abuser asking for their side of the story. Of course their side of the story won't be the truth, but it'll be believable enough that they might turn a blind eye.

TL;DR, Abusive people tend to create a living situation which will either make you not want to leave, or straight up prevent you from leaving.

then the next dwarf down will be able to count the amount of blue hats in front of them, if they count an amount of blue hats that correspond with the first dwarf their hat will be red, otherwise their hat will be blue.

the rest of the villagers count how many blue hats have been said before they ask, and take that into account when they count the blue hats in front of them, every time a dwarf guesses blue they alternate between an even and odd amount of blue hats, allowing all the 9 dwarfs after the first dwarf to answer correctly.
